understand.concept: math.h declares mathematical functions such as sqrt, pow, exp, log, sin and floor. Functions may have domain and range restrictions and can raise floating-point exceptions or set errno depending on the implementation and operation.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct numerical code validates domains, handles exceptional results and avoids assuming exact floating-point arithmetic.

explain.narrative:
math.h declares mathematical functions such as sqrt, pow, exp, log, sin and floor. Functions may have domain and range restrictions and can raise floating-point exceptions or set errno depending on the implementation and operation.

Use authoritative declarations and documentation, state assumptions explicitly and verify behaviour with focused examples. Where the implementation or C version matters, record it.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: sqrt is called only after the simple nonnegative-domain check. The result is a double and is printed to three fractional digits.

practise.guidedTask: Identify the domain restriction for sqrt and log.
practise.independentTask: Create a numerical helper that validates input and handles non-finite results using isfinite where supported.
hints: Floating-point calculations may round and should not be compared as exact decimal values without a defined tolerance.
Some math operations have implementation-defined or documented error reporting through errno and floating-point exceptions.
